title: Towers of Hanoi
domain: Nonnegative integer disk counts with named source, target and spare pegs.
description: Print the recursive move sequence for the Towers of Hanoi. Each line is 'source -> target'; the proposed Glon example uses pegs A, C and B. The exact sequence, move count and legal-disk invariants are verified against an independent Python reference for 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 10 disks.
attribution: Problem and REBOL reference: Rosetta Code, 'Towers of Hanoi' (https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Towers_of_Hanoi). The REBOL listing is the solution shown on that page; the Glon implementation is the proposed Glon version.
reference: Expected output is the exact move sequence produced by the standard independent Python recursive reference. Local verification also simulates the pegs to check move count 2^n-1, no larger disk on a smaller disk, and complete transfer to the target; the committed cases compare the exact stdout.
family_note: Rosetta Code challenge; separate from REBOL Cookbook challenges.

cases.reference: 1023 moves for 10 disks; exact sequence generated independently by the standard Python Towers of Hanoi reference (expected 2^n-1 = 1023).

known_limitations: The challenge tests 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 10 disks. No resource limit was encountered at 10 disks; larger counts were not pursued.
Recursive activation depth is proportional to the disk count; very large counts may exceed the pinned interpreter's resources.
Peg names are application-level strings; the implementation does not validate that they are distinct.

reference_implementation.title: Towers of Hanoi — REBOL solution shown on Rosetta Code
reference_implementation.attribution: Rosetta Code, Towers of Hanoi, REBOL solution (https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Towers_of_Hanoi).
reference_implementation.notes: REBOL 2 function with a /poles refinement and default left/middle/right peg words; the example moves four disks.

rebol.observable_behaviour: Prints the recursive move sequence, defaulting to left -> middle/right peg names and demonstrating four disks.
rebol.facilities: func with a refinement, if/return, recursive calls, words and print from REBOL 2.
rebol.test_status: The original listing is preserved verbatim as reference source. It was not executed here; there is no REBOL 2 runtime in this repository.

glon.observable_behaviour: Prints 'source -> target' lines for the supplied peg names; verified exactly for 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 10 disks.
glon.facilities: Ordinary Glon func/either, comparison and arithmetic, s/+ and s/print; no refinements or new vocabulary.
glon.test_status: 7/7 exact-sequence cases passed on the pinned interpreter; local simulation also checked move count, legality and complete transfer.

implementation_comparison.notice: Both listings are application-level recursive definitions. REBOL uses a refinement to select peg names; Glon passes three string arguments explicitly. Source sizes are descriptive, not a concision claim.
